text:
alice: Heads up — in us-west-2 we keep seeing streaming RPCs getting stuck in the front-end queue for ~6-12s and then timing out. Non-stream bulk/transform jobs are filling the edge pools and starving the streaming slots.
ben: Which pool? edge-gpu-pool-3? any recent scaling events?
alice: edge-gpu-pool-3 and edge-gpu-pool-7. No scale events; the autoscaler is at max because of long-running batch quant jobs. Queue depth spiked: `queue_depth: 142` and streaming inflight went down to 0.
infra-monitor: alert: streaming-latency-us-west2 > 2s for 5m. top offenders: /v1/generate/stream (95% of queued).
carmen: We knew batch would crowd the pools. Two quick options: 1) strict admission priority for streaming so they jump the queue, or 2) reserved soft tokens (% of concurrency) for streaming clients. Preemption for blocky batches is also possible.
sam: Preemption means killing in-progress batch work — costy and user-visible. I prefer reserved tokens + burstable spare capacity.
ben: Cost note: reserving 20% of GPU concurrency for streaming drops batch throughput and increases per-token infra cost. We need a dynamic policy that only reserves when streaming tail latency is > target.
carmen: Agreed. Proposal: dynamic reserve that looks at moving window of streaming P50/P95 and uses token-bucket weight ratios. Rough sketch:

```json
{
  "admission": {
    "policies": [
      {"name": "streaming", "weight": 100, "reserve_pct": "dynamic(0.05,0.25)"},
      {"name": "interactive", "weight": 70},
      {"name": "batch", "weight": 10}
    ],
    "preemption": {"enabled": false}
  }
}
```

alice: That looks reasonable. Also we should avoid full preemption at first — instead mark long-running batch requests as "evictable" with a graceful checkpoint so we can resume.
ben: Can we implement admission as two queues per pool (priority + best-effort) and then have a small fastpath for streaming RPCs that bypasses the best-effort queue? If so we can tune sizes per region.
sam: Yes. Implementation plan: per-node admission token counters, counters exported to telemetry, and a control plane controller that adjusts reserve_pct per pool. We'll need a safe fallback: if controller fails, revert to current config (no reserve).
ben: I'll add a k8s ConfigMap for the canary. Example apply: `kubectl apply -f admit-config-staging.yaml`
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: admitted config applied to staging (admit-controller v2.4.1)
ben: Pushed canary to 10% of edge-pool nodes in staging. Monitor streaming_p95, queue_depth, gpu_util.
car men: @carmen: small nit — streaming clients maintain KV caches; preempting can blow caches and increase cold token cost. Evictable with checkpointing is important.

sam: For metrics, watch: `streaming_p95_ms`, `batch_evictions`, `gpu_active_slots`, `queue_depth_by_priority`. If streaming_p95 improves without big drop in gpu_util, we proceed to prod canary.

alice: Also saw some network flapping on node N-7 at ~1862341200 causing a perf dip. We should isolate that node from canary pools.
ben: Good catch. We'll exclude N-7. Setting canary pool to nodes with stable network.
carmen: One more tradeoff note — reserving tokens reduces tail cost but increases idle slots unless we allow burst borrowing from batch when streaming is quiet. That fits dynamic reserve approach.
ben: Plan for today:
- implement two-queue admission on staging (ben)
- dynamic reserve controller + telemetry dashboards (sam)
- marking batch jobs evictable with checkpoint hooks (carmen)
- run 48h staging canary, then 2% prod for 24h, then ramp (alice)

alice: I'll draft a short postmortem if the prod canary has regressions. For now, rolling to staging.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolling canary to staging pool set (10% nodes) — watch streams.
infra-monitor: FYI: cost estimation if reserve_pct=15% permanently => ~+8% infra cost for batch throughput reduction.
sam: TL;DR: prefer dynamic reserve with burst borrowing + checkpointable evictions. Start small.
alice: Thanks all. If streaming still suffers in 2h, we'll revert and iterate. :thumbsup:
